chapter_note: Substantial substrate teaching organized in three systematic sections: (1) seven goods of the sun contrasted with seven evils of the night (¶5-11, ¶14-20), (2) five archetypes of the sun (¶23-27), (3) three qualities corresponding to the mystery of the Father (¶30-32). The oldest teaching layer is dominant. Editorial bridges are interspersed at section transitions (¶3, ¶12, ¶21, ¶33) polemicizing against 'the sects' for not recognizing these cosmic mysteries. The chapter closes with a Gospel of Thomas citation (¶36) and classic exhortation/beatitude closure (¶37-38), confirming the editorial fatigue pattern flagged by the computational analysis. Low substrate vocabulary scores throughout reflect the absence of this chapter's key terms (sun, night, light, darkness) from the substrate marker list (which targets zoomorphic/metal/taste correspondences), NOT the absence of substrate content. The 7+7+5+3 enumeration structure is the teaching's skeleton. Gardner/McBride's suggestion of heliolatry native to Egyptian Manichaeism may be true at the compilation level, but the correspondential structure (sun as sign of the light-realm, night as sign of Darkness) belongs to the older substrate layer.

paragraphs.core_text: the greatness of the sun and its divinity: how was it fashioned after the likeness of the first greatness?
paragraphs.removed_material: Dialogue frame removed: 'Once again, the apostle is sitting down among the congregation of his disciples, one time, and the sun shone forth. He began to recount to his disciples about' and 'He was revealing to them.' — formulaic scene-setting and attribution.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Dialogue frame formula wraps a substantive cosmological question. The question 'how was it fashioned after the likeness of the first greatness?' defines the teaching structure — the sun as a likeness/correspondence of the First Greatness. This is the Persian pedagogical tradition: the question IS the substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: it is the gate of life and the vessel of peace, to this great aeon of light [...]. it is the gate of the souls' departure
paragraphs.removed_material: 'He says,' — dialogue frame attribution. 'However, since Satan knows that... he placed an exclusionary judgement in his law that no one worship it, saying: Whoever will worship it can die. He has otherwise called it: The light that will be nullified. He has hindered the souls from themselves turning their faces towards the light. He has caused them to deny the light of their being.' — anti-OT polemic referencing Deuteronomy's prohibition of sun worship. This editorial layer reaches outside the cosmic system to identify 'Satan' with the OT God and his 'law' with Deuteronomy. The cosmological claims (gate of life, vessel of peace, gate of souls' departure) are embedded in and used by this polemic but pre-exist it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Two substrate teachings extracted: (1) sun = gate of life and vessel of peace, connected to the aeon of light; (2) sun = gate of souls' departure. Both map cosmos→cosmos. The anti-OT polemic identifies the OT God as 'Satan' — a Manichaean editorial layer that uses these substrate facts as ammunition. Note the OT citation in the footnotes (Deut. 1) confirming the editorial bridge to biblical material.

Pure editorial lamentation about human blindness. 'Now, people are blind about everything!' opens with editorial voice. 'even today' anchors to the editorial present. 'Behold: How many are the charities that it does for mankind!' — rhetorical editorial exclamation. No substrate teaching content; the paragraph is the editor's commentary on human ignorance rather than the teaching itself.

paragraphs.core_text: Every day, would this great light-giver shine its light, it shall do seven good things for them.
paragraphs.removed_material: 'Shall they not see them?' — editorial rhetorical question addressed to the audience, consistent with the editorial voice of ¶3. The structural announcement of the seven-fold teaching is substrate.
paragraphs.temporal_note: This is the structural announcement of the seven-fold enumeration. 'Seven good things' defines the teaching skeleton. The rhetorical question is the editor's voice echoing ¶3's lamentation about blindness.

paragraphs.core_text: The first good thing that it does for them is its light, which it shines upon them. It opens the eyes of all mankind. They see underfoot as they walk by it. It takes away the blindness of the night, which made them blind with its darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First enumeration in the seven goods of the sun. Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system: sun's light → removes night's darkness, opens eyes. The enumeration marker 'The first' is substrate structure.

paragraphs.core_text: The second: When (the sun) is come to the world, with its coming it shall bring calm and peace to the entire world. With its coming it shall also take away from them all the fear and trembling, which their heart is filled with the whole night; for it shall take away the darkness present by its light, and sweep it out. Also, this is how it extinguishes fear by its calm.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second enumeration. Sun → peace/calm, removes night's fear/trembling. Cosmos→cosmos throughout. The teaching describes what the sun IS and DOES as a cosmic force.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is its vigil; because when (the sun) comes to the world all sleeping mankind shall arise and awake. And the watchmen too shall cease from watching. The guards who sit at the gates of camps, they break vigil at the watchposts, because of its light that has shone upon them in the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third enumeration. Sun → awakening/vigil. 'The guards who sit at the gates of camps' describes social effects but as part of the systematic teaching about what the sun DOES. These are cosmic effects, not contemporary institutional references.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.160⟩ The fourth: It shall nourish, and give strength, taste and scent, to the trees and fruits and vegetables, and all the herbs, and the flowers and grasses, which are upon the entire earth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth enumeration. Sun → nourishment of the vegetable kingdom. Note the substrate vocabulary: 'taste and scent' — these are the same sensory-quality registers found in the five-worlds teaching (Ch.6). Sun gives these qualities to vegetation — cosmos→cosmos.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth: When (the sun) shines in all the world, the evil reptile and the sharp-toothed beasts that are filled of wickedness, they shall flee to hiding in their dens.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth enumeration. Sun → driving creatures of Darkness into hiding. The 'evil reptile and the sharp-toothed beasts' belong to the dark-world fauna — cosmic entities, not social categories.

paragraphs.core_text: The sixth: When it shines its light, the wound of any person is eased from pain. Its light shall melt away the evil arts of every doer of wickedness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Sixth enumeration. Sun → healing and dissolution of evil arts. 'Melt away the evil arts' uses the same process-vocabulary found in substrate descriptions of light's action on darkness. Cosmos→cosmos.

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh: (The sun) shall display and manifest to the world the sign of the splendour of the aeons of light, from which it has come out; it here in this world being their sign. It brings light to the whole of creation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Seventh and culminating enumeration. Sun = sign of the aeons of light. This is the correspondential principle stated explicitly: the sun in THIS world is the SIGN of the light-realm from which it emanated. Substrate score 6.98 confirms — 'aeons of light' triggers the vocabulary marker. Both sides within the cosmic system.

Editorial polemic against 'the sects of error.' 'Behold: How great is the foolishness that has befallen the sects of error!' — one side of the mapping reaches into the editorial present ('the sects'). Editorial bridge vocabulary score 8.33 confirms. Structurally, this is an editorial bracket between the seven goods of the sun and the seven evils of the night.

paragraphs.core_text: it has all wickednesses therein. Every occasion, would the night fall, it shall do seven evils in the world.
paragraphs.removed_material: 'Now, just as I have shown you the sun, which does seven good things in the world, hear also what I teach you about the night, for' — first-person editorial transition. 'I have shown you... hear what I teach you' is Mani's editorial voice recapitulating and transitioning. The structural announcement of the night's seven-fold teaching is substrate.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Bridge connective detected. The first-person transition voice ('I have shown you... hear what I teach you') is editorial framing that connects the two seven-fold lists. The substrate content preserved announces the night's seven evils, parallel to ¶4's announcement of the sun's seven goods.

paragraphs.core_text: The first wickedness that the night shall do in the world is the darkness, with which it shall fill the entire world; because when the sun sinks from the world and draws to it its rays, at that instant the shadow of the night shall spread out over the whole world. The eyes of the people fill with blackness. They neither see nor wonder with their eyes, because of the darkness of the night which shall fill the whole world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First enumeration of night's seven evils, directly parallel to ¶5 (sun's first good = light). Night → darkness, blindness. The process description ('when the sun sinks... draws its rays... shadow spreads out') is systematic substrate process-vocabulary.

paragraphs.core_text: The second evil thing that the night shall do is its fear; because when its shadow looms forth, its fear and its trembling shall possess all of mankind. The entire world shall fill of the night.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second evil, parallel to ¶6 (sun's second good = peace/calm). Night → fear/trembling. Cosmos→cosmos.

paragraphs.core_text: The third: When the night falls, all creatures take up revolt. They rebel in their heart, to do wickedness and perdition.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third evil, parallel to ¶7 (sun's third good = vigil/awakening). Night → rebellion/revolt of creatures. Cosmos→cosmos.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth: The heaviness of sleep shall lay upon them, and they fall asleep; they slumber and doze, and they are like these corpses in the night.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth evil. Night → sleep as death-likeness ('like corpses'). This is correspondential language: sleep in the night corresponds to death/unconsciousness in the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth is its ugliness; again, when the night would fall, the form of the people shall be hidden in the darkness and the ugliness of the night. The beauty and the form of men and women shall not be displayed before one another, because of its darkness and its ugliness, which it shall spread out over all their forms.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth evil. Night → hiding of beauty/form. The language of 'form' (morphe) being hidden by darkness is correspondential: beauty/form belongs to the light, darkness hides it.

paragraphs.core_text: The sixth occasion is when the night would fall on the world. At that instant evil people shall come out to do wickedness; the adulterers, and the robbers and poisoners. The evil beasts shall come out, and all the reptiles that are filled with wickedness, from their dens. And they stalk in the night. Also, the demons and fiends find power to do wickedness in the night. Again, the blows and buffets and wounds and discharges shall torment people in the night; because in it the whole of evil shall find strength.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Sixth evil — the longest enumeration. Night enables a four-level hierarchy of wickedness: (1) evil human behavior, (2) beasts/reptiles, (3) demons/fiends, (4) physical afflictions. While 'adulterers, robbers, poisoners' names social types, these function as part of a systematic cosmic description of what night enables across all levels of being — not as identification of contemporary targets. The hierarchy itself (human → animal → demonic → physical) is substrate structure.

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh: The night shall display the sign of the Darkness, its father. It has arisen out of its essence; because this night that came out of this first Darkness has been displayed in the world. Note this night, the shadow of this first Darkness, the one that is entwined and bound in all things above and below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Seventh and culminating evil, directly parallel to ¶11 (sun = sign of light-realm). Night = sign of the primordial Darkness, its 'father.' Substrate score 6.9 confirms. This is the correspondential principle for the dark side: the night in this world is the shadow/sign of the first Darkness. 'Entwined and bound in all things above and below' is cosmic process-vocabulary. Darkness capitalized as personified cosmic entity (functioning as father/origin).

Editorial seam detected. 'Behold, I have taught you about these seven wickednesses' — first-person editorial summary. 'The sects have not seen this black night: what it is; nor from whence is its essence' — polemic against the sects, one side reaching into the contemporary religious landscape. Structurally parallel to ¶12 (editorial bracket after the seven goods). Classic editorial bridge: summarizes substrate teaching, then polemicizes.

paragraphs.core_text: There are five archetypes occur in the sun, it making them [...] as it finds the world.
paragraphs.removed_material: 'Once again he ramified. He says to his disciples:' — dialogue frame attribution. Must be stripped per extraction rules.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Dialogue frame wraps the structural announcement of the five archetypes. The teaching content — five archetypes in the sun — defines the next teaching sequence. The lacuna [...] preserves manuscript damage.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.162⟩ The first is its light; for it illumines by its light the world, and all the creatures who exist in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First of five archetypes. Sun → light → illumination of all creatures. Cosmos→cosmos. Clean enumeration structure.

paragraphs.core_text: The second is its beauty; because when it shines, it shall flood beauty and loveliness upon all creatures and everything.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second archetype. Sun → beauty/loveliness. Cosmos→cosmos.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is its peace; for, again, when the sun would shine on the world, all people shall receive affection through it, and give peace to one another.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third archetype. Sun → peace/affection. Cosmos→cosmos. The social effect (people giving peace to one another) describes what the sun's cosmic force produces, not a contemporary institutional reference.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth is the life of the living soul, which it shall release from all the bonds and fetters of heaven and earth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth archetype. Sun → release of the living soul from cosmic bonds. Substrate score 8.7 — 'living soul,' 'bonds and fetters' trigger the vocabulary markers. This is core Manichaean cosmological teaching: the sun as the vehicle that releases trapped light-particles from matter.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth: It gives a strength to the elements; and also it gives a scent and a taste to the entire Cross of the Light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth archetype. Sun → strength to elements, sensory qualities (scent, taste) to the Cross of Light. Note 'scent and taste' — the same sensory-quality registers found in the five-worlds substrate (Ch.6). 'Cross of the Light' (the suffering light dispersed in matter) is cosmic terminology. Cosmos→cosmos.

paragraphs.core_text: its light illumines more than all lights that occur in the world. Also, its beauty is more beautiful than all the beauties of mankind. Again, its peace is more surpassing than all the powers and guards who exist in the world. Its releasing action, by which it releases the living soul, is a full day ahead of all releasing actions! The strength that it gives to its limbs is a great strength, being mightier than all strengths!
paragraphs.removed_material: 'So, you yourselves see that' — editorial address to the audience, breaking the impersonal substrate voice.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic five-fold comparison restating each archetype as surpassing all worldly equivalents: light>lights, beauty>beauties, peace>powers, releasing>releasing, strength>strengths. The structure maps each substrate archetype to a comparative superlative. Both sides stay within the cosmic system. Only the opening 'you yourselves see' is editorial address.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, there are another three archetypes made apparent by the sun, in respect of the mystery of the first greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: 'Once again' here is a structural transition marker within the teaching, not a dialogue frame formula (no attribution follows). The content announces three further archetypes corresponding to the 'mystery of the first greatness' — this defines the correspondence target for the next teaching sequence. Substrate structural announcement.

paragraphs.core_text: The first is the filling up of the disk of its ship; because its ship has filled up every season, and shall not wane at all, the way that the ship of the moon wanes. This continuous filling, by which it is filled, displays the mystery of the Father, the great greatness; from whom all the powers and the gods have come forth. He shall never wane, nor shall lack ever exist in him!
paragraphs.temporal_note: First of three archetypes mapping sun → Father. Sun's permanent fullness (vs. moon's waning) corresponds to the Father's inexhaustible emanation. Both sides cosmic: (1) sun-ship's permanent disk, (2) Father's eternal plenitude. Classic cosmos→cosmos correspondence.

paragraphs.core_text: The second: (The sun's) light surpasses the light of all the stars, and all the lights that occur in the universe; corresponding to the mystery of the light of the Father; for his light surpasses and is greater than the light of his aeons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second archetype. Sun's surpassing light → Father's surpassing light above his aeons. 'Corresponding to the mystery of' is the explicit correspondence formula. Cosmos→cosmos. The word 'corresponding' is the substrate voice naming the mapping operation.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.163⟩ The third: This sun is very high above all else. It surpasses the height of all the mountains and hills that exist upon the entire earth, corresponding to the mystery of the Father of Greatness; for he is high above all the household of his light-earth. Also, because the Father himself is high above all the heights and the mountains of his light-earth. He is 'filled up' in his image [all] the time and every hour from eternity to eternity!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third archetype. Sun's height → Father of Greatness's supremacy above his light-earth. 'Corresponding to the mystery of the Father of Greatness' — explicit correspondence formula again. 'Light-earth' is cosmic geography. The scare-quoted 'filled up' suggests a technical term recognized by the translator, linking back to the first archetype (¶30). Substrate score 3.7 triggers on this cosmic geography.

Editorial summary and polemic. '[Beho]ld the two mysteries I have taught you, O my beloved ones!' — first-person address with exhortation vocabulary ('O my beloved ones'). 'The sects have not seen them in their error!' — polemic against sects. The cosmological content ('the mystery of the light and the mystery of the darkness are displayed daily in the created order') restates what ¶11 and ¶20 already taught — it is editorial recapitulation, not new substrate teaching. Exhortation score 8.77 confirms devotional register.

paragraphs.core_text: The mystery of the first great light is the sun, which is this second light-giver, the one that comes daily to the world. It displays all the marks of its graces, displaying and signifying on its own behalf that it is good, out of the essence of the good. It came from the good Father and appeared in this world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concluding substrate teaching on the sun. Sun = mystery of the first great light = second light-giver. 'Out of the essence of the good' — ontological origin. 'It came from the good Father' — emanation from the Father of Greatness. Both sides within the cosmic system: the sun's presence in the world corresponds to its origin in the light-realm. This completes the sun-side of the dual mystery.

paragraphs.core_text: this night that is made of fear exists after the mystery of the Darkness. Behold too the mystery of its essence! It displays it in the world in all these wickednesses. It displays this mystery daily in the world.
paragraphs.removed_material: 'In contrast,' — editorial connective. 'but the sects know it not in their error. They do not distinguish the mystery of the light from that of the darkness.' — polemic against sects reaching into the editorial present.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Parallel to ¶34 (sun/light), this teaches the night-side of the correspondence. Night = mystery of the Darkness. 'It displays it in the world in all these wickednesses' — the night reveals the Darkness's nature through its effects. Darkness capitalized as personified cosmic entity. The polemic tail against 'the sects' is editorial bridge, removed.

Gospel of Thomas citation. 'The saviour cast an allusion to his disciples' — citation formula. The saying ('Understand what is before your face, and then what is hidden from you will be unveiled to you') is from Gos. Thom. logion 5. However ancient the saying itself may be, it ENTERED THIS TEXT via a 3rd-century Manichaean citation act. 'Hidden from the sects' anchors to the editorial polemical frame. Institutional score 5.56 confirms.

Editorial seam detected. 'Once again the apostle speaks:' — dialogue frame formula reintroducing Mani's voice for the closing section. 'You are the children of the day and the children of the light... the children of the night and the children of the darkness' — applies the substrate day/night teaching to the audience. One side of the mapping (light/darkness) is cosmic; the other ('You') is the audience. The correspondence is being USED to categorize the community. This is application, not teaching.

Classic beatitude/devotional closure. 'Blessed are you, my beloved ones!' — beatitude formula. 'Blessed is he who can know this mystery... inherit life eternal!' — eschatological promise. Exhortation score 29.03 — the highest in the chapter by far. Every diagnostic marker fires: 'Blessed', 'my beloved ones', 'inherit life eternal', direct address. This is the compilers' devotional wrapper, confirming the editorial fatigue pattern (exhortation shift from 0.0 to 3.54 in the second half).
